newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil business heads lament slow pace of reform.
newsitem.headline: Brazil business heads lament slow pace of reform.

text.p: Brazilian industry representatives told President Fernando Henrique Cardoso of their concern over the slow pace of economic reform Thursday, the president of the National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.

"Although Congress made its contribution in 1996, approving on average each month 1.25 bills which help reduce the cost of doing business in Brazil, the process of change in the economy has to be sped up," Fernando Bezerra said.

The government's reform program has ground to a virtual halt in recent months. Bills to shake up the civil service and the pensions system were unveiled nearly two years ago but remain stuck in Congress where opposition to the reforms is fierce.
Another reform, of the tax system, has yet to begin its long journey through parliament and will probably not be touched until 1999, after next year's elections.
Bezerra said he suggested to Cardoso that the government draw up a clear plan for getting the reforms approved. The president agreed to meet with CNI representatives July 1.
"We need to be internationally competitive because otherwise Brazilian society will pay the bill," he said.
